## What the data shows

The window covers **2024-06-01 to 2026-06-01**, with the end date exclusive; the latest included month is **2026-05** [c1]. The total is **45,512 articles** [c1]. This is a count of matched news articles, not unique outlets, audience reach, or the entire universe of news.

For tone, the tool reports **6.2% negative** and **93.7% positive** for matched articles, versus a corpus-baseline negative-to-positive ratio of **0.58**; the topic ratio is **0.07** [c1]. The publisher concentration estimate comes from a recent sample of **230 articles**: top publisher share **2.2%**, top-three share **5.6%**, with **166 distinct publishers** in the sample [c1]. This suggests broad distribution in that sample, not a full-window concentration measure.

The geography panel places **13,202 of 41,633 matched articles (31.7%)**; this means the article is about the resolved place, not that it was published there [c1]. Place attribution can have acronym collisions [c1].

## Verdict
- Answer: The news corpus holds 45,512 articles mentioning "ai agents" from 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31 [c1]. Monthly volume rose from 199 (June 2024) to a peak of 4,883 (April 2026) [c1], and was 3,879 in May 2026 [c1]. The late third of the window carries 4.46 times the early third [c1].
- Decision: Treat AI agents as a fast-growing, mainstream news topic, and size media or monitoring plans on the 2026 level of about 3,600 to 4,900 articles a month [c1]. Coverage is overwhelmingly framed positively, so do not read volume as a measure of scrutiny.
- Confidence: medium - the counts and series are measured and the corpus passed coverage checks [c1]. But the "mention" match is broad, the data end 2026-05-31 (145 days before today), and the tone labels are machine-assigned.
- What would change it: A re-run with window data from June to October 2026, or with a "central" match for the whole series, could change the level or direction.

## What the data shows
- Volume: 45,512 articles in the window 2024-06-01 to 2026-06-01 (exclusive), match mode "mention" [c1].
- Critical flag: 32,257 articles, which is 70.9% of the total [c1] (derived from 32,257 / 45,512). The "critical" flag sits oddly beside the sentiment labels (see Method and limits).
- Tone: 42,616 positive (93.7%), 2,804 negative (6.2%), 76 neutral, out of 45,496 labelled [c1]. The negative-to-positive ratio is 0.07 against a corpus baseline of 0.58 [c1], so this coverage is much more positive than ordinary news [c1].
- Tone drift: the negative ratio rose from 0.02 in June 2024 to 0.10 in May 2026 [c1], so scepticism is growing from a low base.
- Themes (share of labelled articles, lift over corpus) [c1]:
  - Category: artificial intelligence 12.9% (lift 55.0), technology 29.5%, business 22.2%, financial technology 4.7%, software 5.3%, cybersecurity 2.8%, venture capital 2.0% (lift 76.4), customer service 1.1% (lift 57.0).
  - Subcategory, highest lift: multi-agent reinforcement learning (lift 373.4), reinforcement learning frameworks (336.7), customer support and helpdesk systems (187.4), CRM systems (141.4), workflow automation tools (116.5).
  - Tags: agentic ai 2.4%, mcp 1.6%, salesforce 1.1%, llm 1.2%, servicenow 0.7%.
- Organisations (share of labelled articles, lift) [c1]: Salesforce 2,909 articles (5.9%, lift 134.0), OpenAI 3,137 (6.4%, lift 20.2), MCP 2,353 (4.8%), Gartner 1,103 (2.2%), ServiceNow 851 (1.7%), Databricks 299 (0.6%). The labels are machine-assigned and unverified, and "api", "cto" and "iam" appear as organisations, which shows label noise [c1].
- People [c1]: Sam Altman 391 articles (8.8%), Jensen Huang 271 (6.1%), Marc Benioff 269 (6.1%), Satya Nadella 153 (3.5%), George Clooney 201 (4.5%). The Clooney and "Sam Roberts (singer-songwriter)" entries are likely incidental or mis-resolved matches. People labels cover only 4,433 articles [c1].
- Source concentration: in a sample of 230 articles, 166 distinct publishers appeared, the top publisher held 2.2% and the top three 5.6% [c1]. Coverage is spread across many outlets. This is a sample of recent articles with the "central" match, not the whole window [c1].
- Places: the United States 37.1% of placed articles, the UK 7.0%, India 6.8%, the Netherlands 3.7%, Colombia 3.6%, China 3.4% [c1]. Placed_pct is 31.7% (13,202 of 41,633 matched articles) [c1], so about two thirds of articles have no place and the shares describe only the placed minority.

- Change: the first month was 199 and the last was 3,879, with a peak of 4,883 in April 2026 [c1]. The compound annual growth rate is 372.2% over 1.91 years [c1]. The direction is rising [c1].

## Method and limits
- Windows: trends, tone, themes and sources run 2024-06-01 to 2026-06-01 (exclusive), with the last data on 2026-05-31 [c1]. That is 145 days before today (2026-10-23), so nothing from June to October 2026 is covered. Entities and geography stop at 2026-05-01 (exclusive) [c1].
- Match mode: "mention" for the volume, tone, theme and entity counts. This counts articles that name the term anywhere, including round-ups, and so overstates articles that are mainly about agents. The source panel uses a stricter "central" mode [c1]. The 19,969 articles tagged "ai agents" [c1] are a stricter count of 43.9% of the mention total (derived from [c1]). I do not have a central-match monthly series, so the growth rate for focused coverage is not measured here.
- Coverage: the news table passed the row-count checks (107.1% of expected rows), but the tool says this is not proof of ingest completeness [c1]. Rows are articles in the tool's corpus, not all news. The corpus composition may have changed over time, so part of the growth could reflect crawler expansion; this cannot be separated with the data at hand.
- Censoring: the tool censors the newest month at 2026-06-01 because ingest lags [c1]. The May 2026 figure of 3,879 may still be incomplete.
- Labels: entity and place labels are machine-assigned and unverified [c1]. Geography labels for May 2026 are largely unwritten [c1].
- Critical versus tone: 70.9% of articles carry the "critical" flag [c1] while only 6.2% are negative [c1]. The two measures are not defined the same way, and I could not establish what "critical" means. I therefore do not use it as a measure of negativity.
- Sources: the publisher concentration comes from a sample of 230 articles [c1], not the full window.
- Interpretation: the claim that this is mainstream, fast-growing coverage is my reading. The counts are measured. The CAGR of 372.2% [c1] comes from a start near 199 and should not be projected forward.
- Not answerable from this data: the absolute share of all news that is about AI agents; volume after May 2026; the causes of the growth; the true level of criticism.

## References
No external references were used. All figures come from call c1 (news.overview, term "ai agents", since 2024-06-01); news items are listed with date, publisher and URL in the Drill-down section.
